questions.prompt: Which statement best describes pressure in this lesson?

choices.text: Normal force distributed over an area.

questions.explanation: For this foundational model, pressure is the magnitude of normal force divided by the area over which it acts.

questions.prompt: Calculate pressure when a normal force of 200 N acts over 0.50 m^2.
questions.explanation: Using p = F / A gives 200 N divided by 0.50 m^2, which is 400 Pa.

questions.prompt: For the same normal force, select the surface that produces the greater pressure.
questions.altText: Two surfaces receive the same downward force; surface A has the smaller contact area.
questions.explanation: With force fixed, the smaller contact area produces the greater pressure.

questions.prompt: Which SI unit relationship is correct for pressure?
questions.explanation: The pascal is one newton per square metre.

questions.prompt: A press applies the same normal force using a smaller contact face. What does the foundational model predict?

choices.text: Pressure is independent of contact area.

questions.explanation: For fixed normal force, reducing the contact area increases the calculated pressure. This relationship alone is not a complete equipment design model.
